follow-up time: 5 days before delivery or fetal death
exposure: Phase rectified signal averaging (PRSA) on cCTG
abnormal computerized cardiotocography (cCTG) with recurrent decelerations and/or low short term variation (STV)
abnormal cCTG with recurrent decelerations and/or low phase rectified signal averaging (PRSA)
outcome: Composite adverse condition at birth (fetal death, low Apgar score, low umbilical pH, need for resuscitation)
cohort: 367 pregnancies complicated by FGR and/or pre-eclampsia delivered by pre-labor Cesarean section or experiencing fetal death before 32 weeks' gestation
finding: The study found that both low STV and low PRSA on cCTG, particularly when combined with recurrent decelerations, were similarly associated with an increased risk of composite adverse condition at birth in pregnancies complicated by early onset FGR, but not with major neonatal morbidity.
